newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM looking at Hungary for new engine output.
newsitem.headline: GM looking at Hungary for new engine output.

text.p: General Motors Corp said on Monday it was considering building a new car engine at its Hungarian plants that already assemble cars and build engines.
"The decision on where to build the engine should be taken sometime in 1998," Albert Lidauer, managing director of GM's Hungarian plants, told Reuters.
"The engine will be a brand new design, but I can't say anything more, except that we are definitely bidding to build it in Hungary," Lidauer said, following a news conference.
If GM selects Hungary, production of the new engine would take place in the plant's space for assembling Opel Astra cars, Lidauer said.
GM has said that it is looking at new ways to use the car assembly plant, which never has operated above one third of its maximum annual production capacity of 40,000 units.
But the car plant will increase its output starting in September, when it begins supplying painted bodies to an Opel Astra assembly plant in Warsaw, Lidauer said.
Other options for the assembly plant include continuing car assembly or introducing component manufacturing, Lidauer said.
Separately, GM already is testing pilot production of another new engine that it will build in Hungary, but it gave no details about the engine or the launch date for production.
